requirement:
Saved configuration MUST remain distinct from resolved runtime configuration.
Serializing and deserializing a valid configuration MUST preserve its semantic
values, including explicit versus omitted settings. Optional fields MAY be
omitted on serialization; defaults and environment-derived values MUST NOT be
materialized into omitted fields. TOML comments and formatting need not
round-trip.

Loading configuration or running a configured feature MUST NOT rewrite the user
or project configuration as a side effect. Resolved credentials and live runtime
objects MUST NOT enter the serialized data structures. Explicitly supplied
credential values are permitted only in the fields documented by the authoring
feature; credentials resolved from a profile or environment MUST NOT be written
back to configuration.
rationale:
## Obligations and evidence

The implementation and referenced tests satisfy `requirements.configuration.serialization`.

1. **Saved configuration remains distinct from resolved runtime configuration.** `src/config.rs#struct[UserConfig]` and `src/config.rs#struct[WorkspaceConfig]` define the saved representations. `src/config.rs#fn[resolve_authoring_with_workspace_from]` constructs a separate `ResolvedAuthoringConfig`, cloning the selected backend rather than modifying the saved record. `src/authoring/providers.rs#impl[RigProvider]/fn[connect]` constructs live provider objects separately. Tests `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values]`, `tests/configuration.rs#fn[authoring_policy_defaults_to_confirm_and_round_trips]`, and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections]` assert the distinction between saved selections and effective values.

2. **Serialization and deserialization preserve semantic values.** The saved types derive Serde serialization and deserialization, with tagged backend variants and recursive `OptionValue` values. `src/config.rs#impl[UserConfig]/fn[to_toml]` and `src/config.rs#impl[WorkspaceConfig]/fn[to_toml]` serialize those saved types; their respective `parse` methods decode them. Equality-after-round-trip assertions cover both formats in `tests/configuration.rs#fn[user_and_workspace_authoring_tables_round_trip_every_map]`, backend options in `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]`, and explicit credentials in `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_credentials_round_trip_but_diagnostics_and_debug_redact_them]`.

3. **Explicit settings are preserved.** Optional settings remain `Some` rather than being collapsed to defaults. The concurrency and policy tests above round-trip explicit settings, including explicit default policy values. The map round-trip test preserves project selections and the required present-but-empty user `configs` map.

4. **Omitted settings are preserved.** Optional saved fields use `Option` and skip serialization when absent. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[absent_and_minimal_configuration_are_distinct_and_read_only]` checks an absent authoring section; the backend, concurrency, policy, and OpenAI-default tests check omitted settings after effective values have been obtained.

5. **Defaults are not materialized into omitted fields.** Endpoint accessors borrow effective defaults, and `src/config.rs#impl[BackendConfig]/fn[options_json]` adds OpenAI defaults to a separate JSON value. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[backend_configuration_round_trips_without_materializing_defaults]` checks omission of the default Ollama endpoint. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_defaults_are_effective_only_and_explicit_values_win]` checks that effective model and inference-option defaults do not enter saved TOML. The concurrency and policy tests likewise assert omission.

6. **Environment-derived values are not materialized into omitted fields.** `src/config.rs#impl[OllamaConfig]/fn[api_key_from]` and `src/config.rs#impl[OpenAiConfig]/fn[api_key_from]` return owned resolved values through immutable receivers. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[ollama_authentication_resolves_separately_and_rejects_missing_values]` and `tests/configuration.rs#fn[openai_configuration_preserves_model_and_resolves_credentials]` resolve injected environment values and then assert that serialization contains no resolved key.

7. **Loading does not rewrite user configuration.** `src/config.rs#fn[load_user_config]` reads and parses without writing. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[absent_and_minimal_configuration_are_distinct_and_read_only]` asserts byte-preserving loading and that loading an absent file does not create it.

8. **Loading does not rewrite project configuration.** `src/config.rs#fn[load_workspace_config]` and its reachable `workspace_document` helper only read files. `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_discovery_uses_nearest_file_without_merging_or_rewriting_it]` asserts unchanged file contents on successful loading and on a syntax failure.

9. **Running a configured feature does not rewrite user configuration.** Provider construction accepts immutable configuration and stores runtime state separately. `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[ollama_cli_delivers_sources_records_fixme_and_keeps_usage_content_free]` runs the configured feature with environment-resolved authentication and compares the user file's bytes before and after.

10. **Running a configured feature does not rewrite project configuration.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` executes workspace-only authoring and verifies that both project configuration files remain unchanged and no user configuration is created.

11. **Resolved credentials do not enter serialized structures.** Credential resolution returns separate values; `src/authoring/providers.rs#fn[bedrock_sdk_loader]` applies profile, region, or explicit credentials to an SDK loader without changing the saved record. `src/authoring/providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[omitted_bedrock_profile_and_region_use_standard_sdk_resolution]` compares serialization before and after SDK resolution and excludes resolved access and secret keys. The Ollama and OpenAI credential tests cover environment resolution.

12. **Live runtime objects do not enter serialized structures.** The saved configuration types contain saved scalar, collection, and credential values, not clients or models. Live models reside in the separate `src/authoring/providers.rs#struct[RigProvider]`, which is not serialized. The configured-feature tests exercise runtime construction while asserting unchanged saved files; the effective-default tests also serialize saved values after runtime resolution operations.

13. **Explicit credential values are permitted only in the authoring feature's documented fields.** `src/config.rs#struct[BedrockCredentials]`, `src/config.rs#struct[OllamaConfig]`, and `src/config.rs#struct[OpenAiConfig]` use the credential fields documented by `requirements.authoring.credentials` and `requirements.authoring.configuration_structure`. `SecretString` serializes explicit supplied values normally. The explicit-credentials round-trip test covers all three backends and the optional session token.

14. **Profile-resolved credentials are not written back.** The Bedrock SDK-resolution test verifies unchanged serialized configuration and absence of both resolved key components.

15. **Environment-resolved credentials are not written back.** The separate-resolution unit tests verify their absence from serialized TOML, and the environment-authenticated CLI test verifies unchanged on-disk user configuration.

All tests cited above carry a `{test}` reference to the subject. The optional-field serialization permission imposes no additional obligation, and comments or formatting are expressly outside round-trip preservation. No acknowledged or unacknowledged gap was found.
